entry.title: Merging PDFs in the browser with pdf-lib (no server upload)
entry.summary:
Most online PDF mergers upload your file to a server. For sensitive documents, that's a problem. Use pdf-lib in the browser: Read files with File.arrayBuffer()
PDFDocument.load() each source copyPages() into a new PDFDocument
save() and download via a Blob URL The PDF never needs to leave the user's device for this flow. Open DevTools → Network, merge a test PDF, and confirm there's no upload request carrying the file body. After the app loads, you can even try offline. I packaged this (merge, split, and more) in PDFCraftify: Merge tool: https://pdfcraftify.com/merge-pdf
Guide: https://pdfcraftify.com/guides/merge-pdf-without-uploading
Tradeoffs
Browser memory limits very large jobs Password-protected PDFs must be unlocked first Not a replacement for full desktop DTP If you build similar tools, what edge cases bite you most? Comments welcome.

entry.title: I built a blogging platform where you have to type every word by hand
entry.summary: I got tired of wondering whether anything I read online was written by a person. So I built MadeByHumans (https://madebyhumans.diy), an experimental blogging platform with one rule: you literally have to type your posts by hand. How the proof works: the editor listens to your typing. Rhythm, pauses, backspaces, corrections, all of it gets folded into an effort score for the piece. Pasting is capped at 100 words at a time and 300 total, so you can't just dump text into the box. Then the fun part: readers can hit play on any post and watch a timelapse of the draft coming together. Every clumsy edit and second thought, visible by time of day. There's also an optional 60 second voice intro, and an embeddable badge that carries the effort proof to other platforms. Honestly it started as a reaction to AI slop. But it turned into a more interesting question: what does "proof a human wrote this" even look like? Keystroke dynamics turned out to be a decent proxy. Nobody fakes their way through 300 words of backspaces and 2am rewrite sessions. It's free, no ads, solo built, and real people are publishing on it already. Come poke around if you're curious. Genuine question: does this read as convincing proof to you, or a gimmick? What would make you trust it?
